message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Conformance

on:
  push:
    branches: [ master ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ master ]
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  toml-test:
    name: toml-test ${{ matrix.toml-version }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        toml-version: ['1.0.0', '1.1.0']

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Ruby
        uses: ruby/setup-ruby@v1
        with:
          ruby-version: '4.0'
          bundler-cache: true

      - name: Set up Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version: '1.22'

      - name: Cache Go module dependencies
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/go/pkg/mod
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-go-mod-1.22-toml-test-v2.2.0
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-go-mod-

      - name: Install toml-test
        run: go install github.com/toml-lang/toml-test/v2/cmd/toml-test@v2.2.0

      - name: Make decoder executable
        run: chmod +x tool/toml-test-decoder

      - name: Run toml-test (${{ matrix.toml-version }})
        run: |
          version="${{ matrix.toml-version }}"
          short="${version%.*}"  # 1.0.0 -> 1.0
          skip_file=".github/toml-test-skip-${short}.txt"
          skips=$(grep -v '^[[:space:]]*#' "$skip_file" | grep -v '^[[:space:]]*$' | paste -sd, -)
          echo "Skipping: $skips"
          "$(go env GOPATH)/bin/toml-test" test \
            -decoder ./tool/toml-test-decoder \
            -toml "$version" \
            -timeout 10s \
            -skip "$skips" \
            -skip-must-err
",
  "rationale": "The workflow repeatedly downloads the toml-test Go module via `go install ...@v2.2.0` on every matrix run with no dependency cache, while Ruby gems are already cached. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern (observational evidence; reported modest vm-time reduction) supports caching dependency downloads when repeated fetching is measurable and cache inputs are pinned. Adding an `actions/cache@v4` step for the Go module cache, keyed by runner OS, Go version, and the pinned tool version, reuses the downloaded module across runs without changing any build or test step, coverage, or permissions. No equivalent Go cache exists and the cached content is version-pinned, so no contraindication applies.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE"]
}
